title: The back door comes late: four shorter regular sectors climb first, SOL-82 comes online at sector 3, the door falls once everything is unlocked (sector 6 at the earliest, 8 at the latest), BOTH WALLS follows it, and SKIP ALL starts sector 1 on the finished base
context: Owner, 2026-10-01: "Backdoor wave too aggressive. Let's delay it. First we run more regular waves. Ramp up the difficulty. Then after 4 waves there's a « side breach » ... still within range of some of the existing towers so easier to manage. This is a chekov's gun of sorts, it reveals that the walls can be breached. The backdoor breach comes towards the end, once the player has unlocked all options." Asked, he chose: four sectors, shorter; the back door when everything is unlocked with a latest sector; SOL-82 mid-ramp at sector 3; SKIP ALL at sector 1 on the finished base. Then: "go ahead, push each sector change when green". Before, sector 2 was the back door (feast and scramble, SOL-82 online), sector 1 foreshadowed it, sector 3 was BOTH WALLS and THE COLONY HOLDS came after it, and SKIP ALL opened at sector 2. This is the first of the steps; the side breach is the next.
outcome: src/content/sectors.js: SECTORS is the fixed opening, five gate-side sectors of four pulses (THE LANE 1.2, THE LONG LANE 1.5, THE SKY ANSWERS 1.8 with SOL-82, THE PRESS 2.1, THE NEAR RING 2.2, which the side breach replaces next). Past them SECTOR_HOLD sectors (gate side, +0.15 threat a sector) run until the door is due. SECTOR_DOOR { earliest 6, latest 8 }: at each sector's start src/domain/sectors.js backDoorNext decides whether the next is the door, yes once everything is unlocked (every landing site's part home and Isao's programme printed but for the back gate, which needs the door; read in src/fx/sector-run.js) or at latest. The door is BACK_DOOR_SECTOR (the feast and scramble as before, threat 2.6 from ladder 5) and BOTH_WALLS_SECTOR follows it (threat 2.4, hard cores); THE COLONY HOLDS comes after BOTH WALLS; the generator follows BOTH WALLS. sectorDef takes the schedule (arc). The omens (BACK_OMENS sector 'before') rumble in the sector the schedule put before the door. STORY_SKIP.sector 1; readStoryQuery's firstSector reads ?sector=N on a skip route, and a first sector at or past earliest is the door: the drawer's new BACK DOOR jump is ?skip=defence&sector=6. Isao's sector_hold, sector_door and sector_both lines; skip_defence no longer promises the back door or SOL-82. Every peak is under the 520 frame budget through the first generated sector with the door at 6 or 8 (test/sectors.mjs).
alternatives: A fixed back-door sector: simpler, but the owner asked for the door once everything is unlocked; the floor keeps a run that skips expeditions from never seeing it.
Deciding the door at its own start: the omens need the sector before it, so the schedule decides one ahead.
evidence: npm test (test/sectors.mjs, test/sector-run.mjs, test/back-omens.mjs, test/sector-stats.mjs, test/nav-content.mjs rewritten for the arc), npm run check, npm run architecture.

Browser --sectors (sector 1 quiet, sector 2 THE LONG LANE on the gate side, secured), --skip-tutorial (SKIP ALL at sector 1 on the lane, SOL-82 offline, secured, CONTINUE to 2; the BACK DOOR jump opens the door, the feast, both breaches, SOL-82 online), --phone, --back-gate, --backdoor, --chapters, --grow and --pacing green.
--pacing (ideal defender): sector 1 card 269.1 s, first contact 22 s, 119 arrivals over 70 s (was 290 over 111 s at six pulses and threat 1.5); sector 2 card 364.1 s, first contact 26.8 s.
